question:
Unpolarised light of intensity $I_0$ is incident on a system of two polaroids. The angle between their pass axes is $45^\circ$.
(i) Find the intensity after the first polaroid.
(ii) Find the final transmitted intensity after the second polaroid.
(iii) Explain why the intensity changes at each stage.

options.A:
(i) After the first polaroid, $I_1=I_0$.
(ii) After the second polaroid, $I=I_0\cos45^\circ=\dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt2}$.
(iii) Both polaroids transmit all vibration components.
options.B:
(i) $I_1=\dfrac{I_0}{4}$.
(ii) $I=\dfrac{I_0}{8}$.
(iii) The first polaroid absorbs three-fourths of unpolarised light.
options.C:
(i) $I_1=\dfrac{I_0}{2}$.
(ii) $I=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos45^\circ=\dfrac{I_0}{2\sqrt2}$.
(iii) The second polaroid transmits the component parallel to its pass axis without squaring the cosine factor.
options.D:
(i) The first polaroid transmits half the intensity of unpolarised light, so $I_1=\dfrac{I_0}{2}$.
(ii) The second polaroid acts as an analyser: $I=I_1\cos^2 45^\circ=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\times\dfrac12=\dfrac{I_0}{4}$.
(iii) The first polaroid selects one transverse vibration component; the second transmits only its component along its own pass axis.
